name: Ashveil Duskwalk Crowd-Runner Rig
description: Built for the runner who needs to disappear into a Tier 2-3 crowd and stay there for hours, this rig leads with a structured overshirt in deep forest green with a subtle woven texture — wide enough in the shoulders to conceal a subdermal rig, loose enough in the torso to break the silhouette of body armor. The overshirt has six interior pockets arranged in a deliberate pattern: two at chest height for flat storage, two mid-torso with reinforced magnetic closures for weapon retention, and two low-hip for tools or extraction gear. The back panel is a single sheet of scanner-resistant thermal-baffled fabric that reads as a normal cotton blend to passive scanners. Beneath it sits a dark teal long-sleeve base layer in breathable synth-silk with BCI-port access cuts at both temples and the nape of the neck, sealed with thin magnetic flaps when not in use. The trousers are a straight-leg dark navy workwear twill with hidden waistband storage, articulated knees, and a continuous internal channel along the right thigh for a blade or slim tool. Footwear is a mid-top athletic shoe in muted olive-grey with a split-toe last to accommodate digitigrade or wide geneware feet — the sole has a vibration-dampening layer that kills footstep resonance on metal floors. A slim wrap scarf in dark rust-orange doubles as a face cover, signal-blocking layer when doubled, or an arm sling in an emergency.
functionality: Six-pocket concealment overshirt with weapon-retention mag-closures; thermal-baffled back panel for scanner resistance; BCI-port access cuts with magnetic flaps; continuous blade channel in right trouser thigh; hidden waistband storage; vibration-dampening footwear sole; multi-function emergency wrap scarf; wide-last shoe accommodating geneware feet
what_it_says: Worn well, this reads as a slightly stylish Tier 2 worker — someone with taste but not money. The forest green and dark teal palette is specific enough to look intentional without standing out. The runner wearing this wants to be someone's background, not their memory. They've learned that the best cover isn't a disguise — it's being exactly boring enough.
worn_by: runners with geneware needing inconspicuous footwear
manufacturer: Coldframe Tactical — street label, no fixed address
story_hooks: The runner has been sitting in a Circuit transit hub for four hours running passive surveillance when they realize the wrap scarf's signal-blocking layer has been intercepting encrypted traffic — and they've accidentally collected something that three different corponations would kill to recover.

The overshirt's scanner-resistant back panel passes every checkpoint on the route except one — a newly installed deep-scan arch at a Tier 3 corporate plaza entrance that wasn't on any map the fixer provided.

A contact identifies the runner not by their face but by the specific rust-orange of the wrap scarf, which turns out to be a color associated with a runner crew that was burned six months ago — now every operative in the building is watching.

physical_description.visual_profile: A low-profile, utilitarian silhouette designed for urban concealment. The structured forest-green overshirt creates visual bulk in the shoulders while the loose torso breaks body definition. Layered appearance with visible teal base layer at collar and wrists. Dark navy trousers ground the outfit. Overall impression: a runner prepared for extended fieldwork in dense urban environments, dressed to blend into Tier 2-3 crowds.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized through the shoulders and chest to conceal augmentation hardware and body armor; tapered slightly at the waist to prevent silhouette printing; straight-leg trousers with articulated knee panels for mobility without flare. Base layer compression-fitted at chest and arms. The scarf wraps loose or tight depending on operational need.
physical_description.primary_material: Overshirt: ballistic-weave synth-wool blend with embedded thermal-baffling in back panel. Base layer: breathable synth-silk with BCI-port integration. Trousers: dark twill workwear cotton-hybrid with reinforced stress points. Footwear: composite athletic material with vibration-dampening sole. Scarf: signal-blocking fabric with rust-dyed surface.
physical_description.texture: Overshirt features a subtle woven texture — matte, non-reflective. Back panel reads as smooth, scanner-neutral cotton to passive tech. Base layer has a slight sheen, silk-smooth to touch. Trousers have a structured, workwear nap. Shoe sole textured for grip; upper material slightly padded. Scarf has a tight, dense weave.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep forest green overshirt (primary), dark teal base layer (secondary), navy straight-leg trousers, muted olive-grey footwear, rust-orange wrap scarf. Accents: dark magnetic closures on interior pockets, minimal visible branding.
physical_description.closures: Overshirt: magnetic snap front closure (quiet, fast). Interior pockets: reinforced magnetic catches on mid-torso weapon-retention pockets; standard seams on chest pockets. Base layer: magnetic flaps sealing BCI-port access cuts at temples and nape. Trousers: standard waistband with hidden storage channel. Scarf: wraps and friction-ties; no fixed closure.
distinctive_features: Six strategically placed interior pockets with different retention levels
Thermal-baffled back panel designed to defeat passive thermal scanners
BCI-port access cuts in base layer (temples and nape) with magnetic seal flaps
Articulated knee panels in trousers allowing digitigrade or wide geneware accommodation
Continuous internal thigh channel for blade or tool carry on right leg
Vibration-dampening footwear sole that kills metal-floor resonance
Rust-orange dual-function scarf: face cover, signal-blocking layer, or emergency sling
Split-toe shoe last for non-human foot morphology compatibility
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional streetwear. High-end manufacturing with tactical purpose, but designed to read as working-class urban wear, not luxury. The absence of visible branding and focus on utility over status signals street-level competence.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by runners, infiltrators, corporate security contractors, and urban operatives who need to move through dense crowds without drawing attention. The outfit signals: 'I have augmentations, I carry tools, I know how to stay invisible.' Appeals to people with subcutaneous upgrades and field experience, not showboating corpo elite.
physical_description.condition_typical: When new: pristine, all fasteners secure, scarf pressed. After 4-8 weeks of use: subtle wear at elbows and knees, magnetic closures slightly less crisp, scarf frayed at edges from repeated field wrapping, minor stress creasing at stress points. The garment is built to weather use without looking destroyed.

image_prompt: Cyberpunk fashion photograph of a lean androgynous model wearing the Ashveil Duskwalk rig, standing in three-quarter profile against a rain-slicked GLMZ building facade. The overshirt's forest green catches cool blue neon from a distant corpo billboard while shadows pool in the loose folds of fabric. The rust-orange scarf is loosely wrapped, one end trailing over the shoulder. Visible BCI-port magnetic seals glint at the nape of the neck. The model's hand rests near the right thigh — the internal tool channel subtly visible beneath taut trousers. Split-toe shoes ground the figure on wet concrete. Moody cyan and orange atmospheric lighting. Shot with shallow depth of field; the background is a bokeh of rain, industrial geometry, and distant street noise. Cinematic, street-level, runner aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
